summary.headline: Exide Q4 FY26 revenue grew 9.4% YoY to a record quarter, with EBITDA margin steady at 11.7% despite a ~Rs 150 crore commodity hit.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew about 9.4% YoY and was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with domestic sales up 12.5%. Around 92% of the business, the entire domestic business ex-Telecom, grew about 16%, led by auto OEM (+25% for a second straight quarter). Gross margin fell about 90 bps QoQ to 30.1% on a net material cost hit of roughly Rs 150 crore, but EBITDA margin held at 11.7% sequentially and rose about 50 bps YoY on factory cost, employee cost and warranty savings. Price hikes of about 5-6% across three tranches (January to March) plus about 3% on April 1 are being used to pass through non-lead commodity inflation. In the lithium-ion cell business, the company has invested Rs 4,802 crore in Exide Energy to date, and cylindrical samples are expected to go to customers in May.

financial_highlights.change: Flat QoQ, up about 50 bps YoY

financial_highlights.metric: Cumulative equity investment in Exide Energy Solutions
financial_highlights.change: Rs 600 crore invested in Q4; about Rs 1,500 crore in FY26
Returned to double-digit growth in Q4

segments.name: Auto OEM
segments.commentary: Grew about 25% YoY in Q4, its second consecutive quarter of ~25% growth and highest-ever quarterly revenue. Management expects 20-25% OEM growth to flow into aftermarket after about two years.

segments.name: Home UPS
segments.commentary: Recorded its highest-ever Q4 sales, helped by early summer; FY26 UPS revenue is about Rs 2,300 crore.

segments.name: Replacement (2W/4W)
segments.commentary: Continued mid-teens growth. Auto (OEM plus aftermarket) is about 50% of revenue, with auto:non-auto at roughly 53:47 and auto replacement about 70:30 of auto.

segments.name: Industrial infrastructure ex-Telecom
segments.commentary: Maintained double-digit growth; order inflow and execution healthy in railways, motive power and industrial UPS.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Declined sharply due to geopolitical disruption; now about 5% of revenue, down from about 8% a couple of years ago. Uncertainty expected to persist at least through H1 FY27.

segments.name: Telecom and E-Rickshaw
segments.commentary: Telecom about 2-3% of revenue (E-Rickshaw included in the ~3% estimate), declining as customers shift to lithium-ion.

segments.name: Lithium-ion cells (Exide Energy)
segments.commentary: Pack and module business of about Rs 100-200 crore currently runs on imported cells. Cylindrical NMC line completed internal validation; prismatic LFP line samples targeted for June-July.

guidance_outlook: Management sees the core lead-acid business growing high-single-digit to early-double-digit in FY27, with Q1 FY27 trending similarly to Q4 based on April.
Exports expected to recover in FY27 as geopolitical tensions ease, with a target to regain share toward the earlier ~8% of revenue.
Rs 1,400 crore lithium-ion investment planned in FY27 (capex plus working capital) for Phase-I, per the Board approval.
Non-lead commodity price increases to be passed through quarter-on-quarter; lead governed by formula pricing with OEMs and industrial customers.
Management said it is cautiously optimistic on domestic demand given expected inflation, and will keep cost control tight.
capex_capacity: Lithium-ion Phase-I capacity of 6 GWh in total, split equally: 3 GWh cylindrical (NMC, two-wheeler applications) and 3 GWh prismatic (LFP, for three-wheelers, four-wheelers, buses, telecom and BESS).
Cylindrical line: internal validation complete; customer samples expected in May 2026; customer validation about 2-3 months.
Prismatic LFP line: product trials under way; customer samples targeted for June-July 2026; revenue expected to start earlier than cylindrical because of lighter homologation.
Management targets 85% plant utilisation and 90% yield as the operating benchmarks for cost parity with imported cells.
A separate Hyundai-Kia co-investment is excluded from the 6 GWh and is not yet disclosed; management will disclose it when material.
demand_pricing: Commodity costs rising: sulfur (input for sulfuric acid) rose from about Rs 15/kg a year ago to about Rs 74-75/kg at April exit, against Rs 58/kg at March exit; sulfur up about 40% QoQ in Q4 and about 20% QoQ in the April exit.
Lead is sold at import-parity prices in India, so a ~10% rupee depreciation offset LME softness; LME rebounded to about $1,950 in April.

Price hikes: about 5-6% across three tranches (January 1, March 1, March 20) plus about 3% on April 1, with another round flagged for May-June. Management said OEM price-escalation negotiations are ongoing, with a lag of about one quarter.
Lead, acid and plastic make up about 95-96% of the bill of material; polypropylene plastics hit sharply in Q4 due to crude shortages.

Cell pricing: raw materials currently imported from China, so landed cell cost is higher. Management expects to match imported landed cost via yield, utilisation, localisation, and a 9% increase in Chinese VAT on exported cells (3% now, 6% more by January 2027).

qa_highlights.question: How much commodity cost impact in Q4 and what is the outlook for Q1 FY27, and what price hikes have been taken?
qa_highlights.answer: Net material cost impact in Q4 was about Rs 150 crore, cutting gross margin about 90 bps to 30.1%. Factory costs, employee costs and warranty costs offset it, keeping EBITDA at 11.7%. Price hikes of about 5-6% (three tranches) plus about 3% on April 1 were taken, with further hikes expected.

qa_highlights.question: How much investment is planned for lithium-ion in the next one to two years and how will yields and pricing evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 1,400 crore is planned for FY27 (capex plus working capital), which management considers sufficient for Phase-I. Yield is expected to reach about 90% after three-shift running; localisation and utilisation above 85% are the levers to reach landed-cost parity.

qa_highlights.question: When will cell revenue start, and has there been any revenue commitment?
qa_highlights.answer: Pack and module revenue is about Rs 100-200 crore on imported cells. Cell sales have not started; cylindrical samples go out in May and prismatic samples in June-July. Management will give advance notice of the official start date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sulfur price escalation and how fast is it passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulfur (not sulfuric acid) rose from Rs 15/kg to about Rs 75/kg over trailing four quarters. Price increases on acid are reflected in the same quarter, which is why hikes were taken on March 20 and April 1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 6 GWh capacity split and how does the Hyundai tie-up fit?
qa_highlights.answer: The 6 GWh is split 3 GWh cylindrical and 3 GWh prismatic. The Hyundai-Kia co-investment is separate and would be incremental to the 6 GWh; no commissioning timeline has been disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-current investments fall about Rs 850 crore, and was HDFC Life stake sold?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said no shares were sold. The fall reflects a mark-to-market decline in the HDFC Life holding as of 31 March 2026, routed through OCI with no P&L impact.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (sulfur, polypropylene, lead via rupee, lithium rebound) could keep compressing gross margin; pass-through depends on OEM negotiations with a lag of about one quarter.
Export recovery in FY27 depends on easing geopolitical tensions, with uncertainty expected through at least H1 FY27.
Lithium-ion ramp-up: yield, utilisation, validation timelines, and pricing parity against Chinese imports remain unproven.
Lack of formal government policy support for localised cell manufacturing; management says roughly 15-20 GWh of domestic capacity may be needed before policy intervention.
Rupee depreciation raises import parity pricing for lead and imported cells; monitor the Rs 1,400 crore FY27 lithium-ion capex and the Hyundai-linked capacity disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the core lead-acid business and Q1 FY27, which management says is tracking similarly to Q4. Cautious on commodity costs, export recovery and cell-plant economics, and evasive on lithium-ion pricing, return metrics and the Hyundai-linked capacity, citing material-disclosure status.
key_quotes: And in Q4, we generated our highest-ever quarterly revenue.

But as far as price hike is concerned, I think I have mentioned this in the past that in Q3, we did not take a price rise consciously because the revised GST rates were announced and we thought we would pass on the entire benefit to the end consumer.
So, the short answer is this, that this year, at least quarter-on-quarter, we will pass-through the non-lead price increases to the customers.
Let us ramp up our plant. Let us operate at 85% utilization with 90% yield.

Lithium-ion Phase-I prismatic LFP line, 3 GWh (3W, 4W, buses, telecom, BESS)

growth.why: Management guides core lead-acid business to high-single-digit to early-double-digit growth in FY27 (midpoint ~10%), with Q1 FY27 trending like Q4; backing is partial: price hikes of ~5-6% plus ~3% and auto OEM +25% momentum, while lithium-ion 6 GWh Phase-I (samples May-July 2026, Rs 1,400 cr FY27 investment) is not yet revenue-generating.
